C0.quote: trimming mechanisms that (i) request each player to announce one alternative
C0.note: Aggregation of players' reports into a collective decision via trimmed mean voting mechanisms.

C1.quote: each trimmed mechanism leads, essentially, to a unique equilibrium
C1.note: Main results are a strong Nash equilibrium characterisation and comparative statics, plus a lab experiment. Incentives to misreport (polarisation, weak dominance of sincerity under the median) are also analysed, so SB applies.

C2.1.quote: each player i submits a report si ∈ [0, 1]

C2.2.quote: the strategy space for each player equals S = [0, 1]
C2.2.note: Each input is a single point (location) in the unit interval, integers 1-100 in the experiment, not a cardinal score or utility over alternatives.

C2.3.quote: Each player i has utility function ui in U

C2.4.quote: Under sincere voting, si = pi, and under strategic voting
C2.4.note: Reports si and peaks pi have separate notation.

C3.1.note: The equilibrium and experimental analyses are strategic. Section 4 (Examples 1-2, Tables 1-3) also analyses outcomes under sincere voting as a benchmark.

C3.2.quote: Note that when voting is sincere si = pi .
C3.2.note: The sincere analyses are explicitly defined by si = pi.

C3.3.note: Sincere voting serves only as a comparison benchmark, and no reason is given for voters being sincere.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH (points on the interval), so the applicability condition is not met.

C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by distance to the centre and to the median peak, not by welfare, efficiency or representation.

VOT.quote_behav: Under sincere voting, si = pi , and under strategic voting
VOT.quote_info: Our results were derived in a context of complete information
VOT.note: Strategic in the equilibrium analysis and the experiment; sincere in the Section 4 benchmark. Starting points are common knowledge in the experiment.

DES.note: Mechanism designer is mentioned only outside the formal model.

C8.1.quote: based on the concept of strong (Nash) equilibrium (Aumann, 1959)
C8.1.note: Nash equilibrium is used in Lemma 1; a weakly dominant strategy is used for the median mechanism.

C9.2.note: Needed assumptions are strategic voters, single-peaked held utilities distinct from reports, and complete information; all are stated.

C1.reason: The paper explicitly analyses incentives for strategic misreporting and the weak dominance of sincere voting under the median, which falls under SB alongside EQ and EM.

C2.2.reason: A report is a location in the policy interval, not a cardinal score, utility or valuation, so OTH fits better than CARD.

C3.1.reason: Section 4 explicitly analyses sincere-voting outcomes in worked examples, so not every analysis models strategic voters.

C3.2.reason: For the sincere benchmark analyses the paper states in words that reports equal peaks.

C3.3.reason: No justification is offered for sincere behaviour in the benchmark, so NONE applies.

C6.VOT.reason: Consistent with C3.1 = SOME, voters are strategic in the main analyses and sincere in the benchmark analysis.
